jobs.description: Headquarters: US Remote Senior Director, Revenue Accounting Bitwarden is looking for a Sr. Director of Revenue Accounting to own how we recognize, record, and report revenue across both self-service and sales-assisted channels. This leader is accountable for the full revenue cycle, from contract and invoice through cash and recognized revenue. You will own our revenue stack (Stripe, HubSpot, and Rillet) end to end and partner closely with Sales, Legal, FP&A, and Engineering. What You'll Own: Own end-to-end order to cash operations for both self-service (PLG, credit card, via Stripe) and sales-assisted (enterprise, multi-year, custom contract) revenue streams. Own revenue recognition under ASC 606 for self-service and sales-assisted contracts, including performance obligations, standalone selling price, contract modifications, multi-year and ramped deals, usage-based components, and channel or reseller arrangements. Own deferred revenue, revenue schedules, and the monthly revenue close in Rillet, and deliver accurate revenue results to Corporate Accounting for month-end close. Design billing and revenue processes for large, complex transactions: multi-entity contracts, custom pricing, mid-term upgrades and downgrades, true-ups, and co-terming, from HubSpot deal creation through Stripe invoicing to Rillet recognition. Own the data flow and reconciliation across HubSpot, Stripe, and Rillet, including the bookings to billings to revenue reconciliation, the deferred revenue rollforward, and AR subledger to general ledger tie-outs. Own sales tax compliance across all channels, including nexus monitoring, tax calculation and collection in Stripe, exemption certificate management, return filing and remittance, and audit readiness, in partnership with external tax advisors. Write technical accounting memos for non-standard enterprise contracts and review them with external auditors. Own SOX controls for the revenue cycle and serve as the main contact for audit fieldwork on revenue. Define and monitor KPIs: billing accuracy, days sales outstanding, dunning/failed payment recovery rate, invoice cycle time, and dispute rates. Partner with Sales to structure non-standard enterprise deals so they translate cleanly into accurate, compliant billing in Stripe. Own sales commission accounting and administration, including commission calculations and payouts, ASC 340-40 capitalization and amortization of commission costs, and accrual accuracy, and partner with Sales leadership, FP&A, and HR on commission plan design, quota and attainment rules, and the cost and controls impact of plan changes. Drive Stripe configuration and automation (subscription schedules, proration rules, dunning/failed payment recovery, invoicing rules) to reduce manual touch on high-volume self-service billing. Partner with SalesOps to own the HubSpot-to-Stripe-to-Rillet data pipeline — ensuring deal terms, billing events, and revenue entries stay in sync, and closing gaps with native integrations, middleware, or custom tooling as needed. Collaborate with Product/Engineering on Stripe/product OTC enhancements, new pricing models, and packaging changes. Lead, mentor, and scale a billing, collections and commission teams (analysts, specialists, managers) as transaction volume and deal complexity grow. What We're Looking For: 10+ years of accounting experience, including 5+ years in SaaS revenue accounting and 3+ years leading teams. CPA or equivalent public accounting experience Deep, hands-on ASC 606 experience for SaaS, including large and non-standard enterprise transactions: custom terms, multi-year deals, usage-based or hybrid pricing, amendments, and co-terming. Experience accounting for both self-service (high-volume, automated, credit-card-based) and sales-assisted (contract-based, high-value) revenue. Experience with SOX, external audit management, and building controls in a growing company. Experience managing billing, collections, or order-to-cash teams, and commission Track record of building scalable processes and automating manual workflows, including integrations between CRM, billing, and accounting systems. Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills; comfortable in ambiguity and fast-changing environments. Senior Director, Revenue Accounting

 

Bitwarden is looking for a Sr. Director of Revenue Accounting to own how we recognize, record, and report revenue across both self-service and sales-assisted channels. This leader is accountable for the full revenue cycle, from contract and invoice through cash and recognized revenue. You will own our revenue stack (Stripe, HubSpot, and Rillet) end to end and partner closely with Sales, Legal, FP&A, and Engineering.

 

What You'll Own:

 

  • Own end-to-end order to cash operations for both self-service (PLG, credit card, via Stripe) and sales-assisted (enterprise, multi-year, custom contract) revenue streams.

Headquarters: Remote - Mexico

Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

We are looking for a self-starting, motivated, and experienced Collections Specialist to support the small business globally. The Collection Analyst oversees the accounts receivable efforts of a global portfolio of monthly receivables and acts as the conduit between the sales team, the customer, and corporate. This opportunity requires a candidate with a high volume accounts-centric mindset, high attention to detail, excellent problem-solving abilities, and an enthusiastic attitude. Candidates must have the ability to juggle multiple tasks and priorities, thrive in a highly driven environment, enjoy learning new skills, procedures, and systems, and have an overall desire to contribute to company growth. This position plays an essential role in minimizing our financial loss by implementing receivable and collection procedures that reduce the amount of delinquency encountered and reports to our Sr. Manager, Order to Cash.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in Mexico.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, and countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper-growth environment.
  • You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-caliber team that will encourage you to do your best. 

In this role, you will:

  • Manage a portfolio of global customers
  • Be responsible for updating management on customer payment issues
  • Act as primary AR contact for the sales team
  • Perform consistent collections diligence to ensure timely conversion of past due and current accounts receivable
  • Escalate past due accounts for review and approval for account suspension or when account resolution has not occurred within certain timelines
  • Resolve customer issues preventing payment timely and accurately within prescribed SLA commitments
  • Collaborate cross-functionally to resolve account issues such as pricing, returns, or defective items
  • Reconcile customer accounts to resolve discrepancies caused by misapplied payments or other account issues as needed
  • Maintain account data as needed for accurate customer information
  • Coordinate support and/or resolution for the Account Team (AE or CSM) with questions about billing and contracts or escalate to the Invoice Team when necessary
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s Operating Principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices   

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • Bachelor’s degree, preferably in finance.
  • 2+ years of business-to-business collections experience
  • Fluency in English and Spanish
  • Knowledge of operational accounts receivable processes
  • Excellent customer service skills to provide best-in-class service
  • Must be able to meet or exceed deadlines with a strong attention to detail
  • Strong ability to prioritize and organize work effectively
  • Strong, effective communication skills
  • Must be able to collaborate and communicate effectively
  • Experience with NetSuite, SFDC, and intermediate Excel skills is strongly preferred6
  • Highly organized, self-disciplined, and ability to work in a fast-paced environment
  • Critical thinker, able to implement scalable processes
  • Strong organization skills with exceptional attention to detail and follow-through
  • Experience with SaaS and or technology firms with high volume and growth

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working 

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations 

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email accessibleinterviewing@samsara.com or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/samsara-collections-analyst-i

About the job

We are actively recruiting for this role to fill an existing vacancy. This position will be responsible for working constructively with our customers and partners to resolve billing issues and fraudulent misuse of services. 

We are seeking a sharp, highly data-oriented, and tenacious Fraud Specialist to join our team. Unlike a traditional billing or collections role focused on routine outreach or simple invoice review, this position is a hybrid of financial investigation, root cause analysis, and strategic dispute negotiation.  In this role, you will look for billing discrepancies, investigate Artificially Inflated Traffic (AIT) or IRSF (International Revenue Share Fraud), dig deep into messaging and call data, project manage high-value customer and vendor disputes, and build data-backed cases to resolve discrepancies. You will build dashboards to communicate key metrics and drive action. If you love solving complex data puzzles, negotiating with external parties, and finding win-win outcomes, this is the role for you.

You will be part of a company that is the category leader in Communications Platform as a Service (CPaaS), an organization working with the largest customers and partners, and a team of operators and former consultants that have delivered exceptional impact. If you have an extreme owner / founder mindset and a desire to solve big challenges, you’ll find yourself at home.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll:

  • Advise account managers, accounting, and management on best practices to handle billing disputes
  • Negotiate with customers and carriers with an understanding of resolution levers available as per contractual terms and industry norms
  • Identify, analyze, and handle fraudulent misuse (such as Artificially Inflated Traffic) and billing errors (such as rate differences) with both vendors and customers
  • Own the end-to-end lifecycle of customer and vendor disputes from intake of disputes to initiating disputes, tracking progress, and ensuring timely, documented resolution
  • Uncover and resolve discrepancies, overcharges, and unpaid balances with carriers and customers due to quantities, rates, currency, and other root causes

  • Build dashboards that communicate key metrics related to the lifecycle of disputes

  • Experience in project management.
  • Experience wrangling data with Excel / Google Sheets, Looker or SQL.

Desired:

  • Understanding of the A2P SMS ecosystem, international traffic routing, international revenue share fraud (IRSF), artificially inflated traffic (AIT) and the ecosystem profit chains.

Travel

The successful candidate’s starting salary will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location.

Comfort with production observability and with data-heavy environments (Databricks or equivalent). Evidence of using AI coding agents to ship faster without lowering the quality bar. Strong plus: Experience with conversational or chat UI at scale; LLM tracing tools (LangSmith, Phoenix, Braintrust or similar); prompt versioning or CI-integrated evals; dashboard, charting, or data-visualization products; enterprise SaaS permissions and entitlements; prompt-injection mitigation and output validation. Why this role: You build the Smart Assist experience used by enterprise customers, with real users and a measurable quality bar. You work across the stack, from the interface to the agent tools behind it, so you see your work reach customers end to end. The problems are distinctive: enterprise-grade permissions and security, and one assistant that works across a broad work-management product. You work on the hard parts of production agents, on a team that values engineering rigor and diverse perspectives. Headquarters: -REMOTE, USA-

For over 20 years, Smartsheet has empowered teams to manage work seamlessly and scale solutions smarter. Now, in our most ambitious chapter yet, we are uniting human teams with AI agents. By orchestrating the work agents do best, automating manual tasks and uncovering insights at scale, we create the space for people to focus on what truly matters: judgment, creativity, and big thinking. That is magic at work, and it’s what we show up for every day.

Smart Assist is Smartsheet's AI agent for work management, used by enterprise customers to analyze, create, and act on their work. AI Experiences builds the orchestration for Smart Assist and the user-facing implementations that expose Smartsheet's Intelligent Work capabilities to any AI surface, so users can reach the right intelligence at the right time through a coherent, reliable experience.

AI Experiences is a pillar within Applied AI, and this is a full-stack team. The work spans these areas: the Smart Assist frontend (UI components, interaction patterns, and rendering for AI experiences across Smartsheet); the Smart Assist backend and orchestrator; UX for Smart Assist tools and agents, from response formatting and onboarding to error states. On the backend, the orchestrator routes each request to the right sub-agent based on user intent, keeps conversation state across multi-turn interactions, handles fallbacks when sub-agents are unavailable, and controls feature-flagged rollout of new capabilities. We partner closely with Agent Engineering on much of this logic.

The role. You will own features and components of Smart Assist from prototype to production, across the front end, the orchestrator and back-end services. You will turn ambiguous product asks into reliable, well-measured behavior customers can trust, and work with product, design, and AI Experience to ship.

You Will:

  • Own a core piece of the Smartsheet AI experience, or a significant part of one (for example conversational analytics, chart-to-dashboard creation, or a new entry point into the assistant) from design through production.
  • Build full-stack: user-facing components, the services behind them, and the contracts between the two, with typed APIs, clear error states, and tests.
  • Design and ship agent tools, skills, MCP tools, and MCP Apps with contracts the model can use reliably, and decide when an action belongs in a tool, a service, or the model.
  • Shape how agent output appears to users: streaming responses, loading and failure states, and handling of long or partial results, working with design and product.
  • Build and evolve the Smart Assist orchestrator: intent-based routing to sub-agents, multi-turn conversation state, fallback and degradation handling, and feature-flag rollout of new capabilities, partnering closely with Agent Engineering. Populate the context the agent receives, such as user locale, timezone, and workspace state.
  • Define how quality is measured for your area: build golden cases and scorers, set regression gates, and use traces and production signals to decide whether a failure needs a prompt, tool, context, or UI fix.
  • Instrument features with tracing, structured logs, and latency, cost, and error dashboards, and act on what they show.
  • Take part in on-call, security, and cost work for Smart Assist, shared with Agent Engineering. Reproduce production failures and review code for your team.
  • Partner with PMs, designers, Agent Engineering, AI Platform, MCP, and data teams. Learn how customers use what you build and flag gaps in requirements and tests.
  • Use AI coding tools to ship faster without lowering the quality bar.

What we're building next:

Our goal for the coming year is to make Smart Assist safe to trust and hard to leave. You will help shape work across four themes:

  • Be everywhere: an assistant that understands what you are looking at, such as the rows you have selected, and meets you in the flow of work, including smoother import and file upload.
  • Build the habit: an assistant that remembers how you like to work, with personal, team, and organization profiles, quick commands, and a growing UI component catalog.
  • Earn the trust: previews before changes apply, linked sources and explanations for results, AI edits visible in history and activity logs, and a view into the agent's reasoning.
  • Work together: a directory of agents, @mentions, and the ability to save and share results as pages.

Further out, the vision is a Smart Assist that finds you before you ask: a proactive, insight-first surface that learns how your workspace works, suggests prompts personalized to you, brings in context from tools like Slack, Zoom, and documents, supports multiplayer conversations, and offers help inside the chat itself. You would help define the trust model for that experience from real customer learnings and feedback.

You Have:

  • 2–4 years of professional software engineering shipping production systems.
  • Strong in Python and/or TypeScript/React, with good habits in testing, code review, and debugging.
  • Experience building and shipping customer-facing features end to end, including APIs, data modeling, and user-facing behavior.
  • 1+ years building LLM-powered features in production: tool or function calling, agent loops, prompt and context design, or multi-step workflows.
  • Working knowledge of how agents fail (bad tool choice, context overflow, hallucinated arguments, runaway cost) and how to design around it.
  • Experience designing eval scorers and golden datasets, and using results to make and defend a decision.
  • Experience with MCP tools and MCP Apps, structured tool calling, or reusable agent skills.
  • Comfort with production observability and with data-heavy environments (Databricks or equivalent).
  • Evidence of using AI coding agents to ship faster without lowering the quality bar.
  • Clear communication of quality, cost, and reliability findings to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Legally eligible to work in the U.S. on an ongoing basis.

Strong plus:

Experience with conversational or chat UI at scale; LLM tracing tools (LangSmith, Phoenix, Braintrust or similar); prompt versioning or CI-integrated evals; dashboard, charting, or data-visualization products; enterprise SaaS permissions and entitlements; prompt-injection mitigation and output validation.

What success looks like:

  • First 90 days: ship a feature or improvement to production with eval coverage, and take your first on-call rotation.
  • First 6 months: own a feature or significant part of a project with measured gains in task success, latency, or user adoption, and contribute at least one reusable component or pattern.

Why this role:

  • You build the Smart Assist experience used by enterprise customers, with real users and a measurable quality bar.
  • You work across the stack, from the interface to the agent tools behind it, so you see your work reach customers end to end.
  • The problems are distinctive: enterprise-grade permissions and security, and one assistant that works across a broad work-management product.
  • You work on the hard parts of production agents, on a team that values engineering rigor and diverse perspectives.

We are looking for an experienced, commercially aware, and regulatory-savvy compliance professional to join us as Head of Compliance and Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO).
The role will be instrumental in building the compliance programme from the ground up, and embedding a culture of compliance across the organisation.
Broader team management responsibilities will be added in due course for regulatory strategy, operational execution, and governance.
 
 

What You’ll Be Doing

Regulatory Engagement

  • Serve as the primary point of contact with relevant regulatory bodies.
  • Ensure the organisation meets all applicable governance requirements, including fit and proper obligations for Approved and Designated Persons.
  • Monitor and interpret regulatory developments relevant to virtual assets, and advise senior management and the Board accordingly.

Compliance Programme Development & Management

  • Design, implement, and maintain a comprehensive compliance framework aligned with local requirements, FATF recommendations, and international best practice for virtual asset service providers (VASPs).
  • Develop, review, and update all internal policies and procedures covering AML/CFT, KYC, customer due diligence (CDD), enhanced due diligence (EDD), transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, data protection, cybersecurity compliance, and safeguarding of client assets.
  • Establish and oversee the compliance monitoring programme, including periodic testing, gap analysis, and reporting to senior management and the Board.
  • Prepare and present regular compliance reports to the Board and relevant committees, including on regulatory changes, compliance breaches, and remediation progress.
  • Ensure compliance considerations are integrated into new product design and operations from the inception phase by driving solutions that balance commercial outcomes and innovation, while maintaining a robust compliance posture using a clear risk-based approach.
  • Review technical documentation, user journeys, and product flows to ensure compliance risks are addressed; provide clear, actionable and solution-focused advice during the product lifecycle.
  • Build and scale compliance policies governing advertising, social media campaigns, influencer partnerships, and product launches.
  • Partner with Legal, Product, and Marketing teams to operationalize a timely review process for client-facing assets and go-to-market materials.

AML/CFT & MLRO Duties

  • Act as the designated MLRO, with full statutory responsibility for overseeing the organisation's AML/CFT framework.
  • Receive, review, and assess all internal Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) from staff, and make informed decisions on whether to file external disclosures with competent local authorities.
  • Oversee and continuously improve the transaction monitoring programme, with support from global compliance and product functions.
  • Ensure robust sanctions screening against all applicable lists, including OFAC, UK OFSI, UN, EU, and applicable local sanctions designations.
  • Oversee customer risk scoring, risk-based KYC/CDD processes, and enhanced due diligence for high-risk customers, politically exposed persons (PEPs), and customers from high-risk jurisdictions.

Governance & Culture

  • Act as a key member of the senior leadership team, providing compliance input on new products, services, partnerships, and business initiatives.
  • Champion a strong compliance culture across the organisation through training, communications, and leadership by example.
  • Design and deliver AML/CFT and compliance training programmes for all staff, ensuring completion records are maintained.
  • Ensure that the organisation's compliance obligations are adequately resourced, and advise the Board on staffing, systems, and budget requirements.
  • Establish and maintain a compliance manual, risk register and oversee the escalation and resolution of compliance incidents and breaches.

Reporting & Recordkeeping

  • Prepare and submit all required regulatory reports and notifications to relevant authorities within stipulated deadlines.
  • Ensure that all compliance records, SAR documentation, KYC files, and transaction monitoring records are maintained in accordance with applicable retention requirements.
  • Support and facilitate any inspections, supervisory visits, or regulatory examinations.
 

What We Look For In You

  • Qualifications

    • Bachelor's degree in Law, Finance, Business, or a related field. A postgraduate qualification is advantageous.
    • Professional certification in compliance or AML is strongly preferred (e.g. CAMS, ICA Certificate/Diploma in AML or Compliance, CFE, or equivalent).

    Experience

    • Minimum of 8 years of experience in compliance, AML, or financial crime prevention, with at least 3 years in a senior or leadership compliance role.
    • Demonstrated in-house experience working within virtual asset service providers (VASPs), cryptocurrency exchanges, fintech firms, or regulated financial institutions.
    • Prior experience as an MLRO or Deputy MLRO is highly desirable.
    • Experience engaging directly with financial regulators and the financial intelligence unit
    • Hands-on experience building compliance programmes from the ground up in a start-up or scaling environment is a significant advantage.
    • Familiarity with the regional regulatory framework and requirements is strongly preferred.

    Knowledge & Skills

    • Deep understanding of FATF Recommendations and their application to virtual asset service providers, including the Travel Rule (FATF Recommendation 16)
    • Strong knowledge of crypto-specific AML typologies.
    • Proficiency with blockchain analytics and transaction monitoring tools (e.g. Chainalysis, Elliptic, TRM Labs, or equivalent).
    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and Bahasa Indonesia.
    • Strong analytical and investigative skills, with the ability to identify and articulate complex risk scenarios clearly.
    • Demonstrated ability to engage constructively with regulators, external auditors, and law enforcement.
    • High degree of personal integrity and sound professional judgment.
 

Nice to Haves

    • Experience in cryptocurrency or blockchain compliance programs.
    • Experience working in a multi-national financial institution setting.
    • Familiarity with compliance technology and analytics tools.
    • Prior exposure to multi-jurisdictional compliance oversight.
    • In-depth knowledge of crypto products, including spot trading, derivatives, staking, lending/borrowing, DeFi, and stablecoins.
 

Additional Notes

This role will be subject to fit and proper assessment as part of the licensing process. Candidates must be prepared to undergo background checks, provide regulatory questionnaires, CVs, references, and proof of relevant qualifications. Prior enforcement history, regulatory sanctions, or unexplained gaps in professional record may affect eligibility.
 

Perks & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package
  • L&D programs and Education subsidy for employees' growth and development
  • Various team building programs and company event
  • More that we love to tell you along the process!

Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.
 
OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). What You’ll Be Doing

 
Institutional Client Development & Acquisition
  • Proactively identify and develop high-value institutional clients with significant asset scale and trading potential, including professional investment firms, asset management companies, quantitative trading teams, and family offices.

Deep Relationship Management & Client Lifecycle
  • Develop a thorough understanding of each client's trading strategy, capital structure, and product needs, and deliver tailored service solutions accordingly.
  • Maintain regular and in-depth engagement with clients, foster long-term trust-based relationships, and continuously drive growth in assets under management, trading activity, and platform stickiness.
KPI Ownership & Business Performance
  • Take full ownership of key performance metrics for your client portfolio, including AUM, trading volume, and revenue contribution.
  • Consistently meet monthly and quarterly targets for asset onboarding and business activation, and optimize client value output over time.
Consultative Product Sales
  • Develop deep expertise across the platform's full product suite — including spot, derivatives, structured products, and institution-exclusive services — and provide tailored product recommendations based on each client's investment strategy and business objectives, helping clients optimize returns or achieve risk management goals.
Client Needs Synthesis & Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Gather and synthesize institutional client pain points and customization requests. Coordinate with internal teams across product, risk, compliance, and operations to deliver bespoke solutions for key clients.
  • Proactively provide clients with market insights and professional guidance at critical moments.
Market Intelligence & Competitive Tracking
  • Stay current on institutional crypto market trends and competitor service strategies.

高净值机构客户开发与拓展

机构产品方案顾问式销售

行业洞察与竞品追踪

Headquarters: Remote US

Head of Content

Outmarket AI · Remote (US) · Full-time · Reports to the SVP of Marketing

About Outmarket

Insurance still runs on manual work. Most policies are sold through agents and brokers, and the people who know the work best are buried in the documents: checking policies line by line, comparing quotes, building proposals, on nights and weekends. We think that's backwards. The best people in insurance should spend their time advising clients.

Outmarket, the AI platform built for insurance, makes that possible. Account teams drop in their documents and get back finished work to review, with every finding linked to the page it came from. Outmarket connects to the systems they already use. The judgment stays with the person; the groundwork doesn't.

It's working. More than 10,000 people at over 300 agencies use Outmarket, including 30 of the top 100 U.S. insurance brokers. Most of those agencies found us through other customers. We raised a $34.5M Series B led by SignalFire four months after announcing our Series A because customers were pulling us forward faster than we planned.

Why this role

  • Customers who want to talk. About 300 agencies use Outmarket, and most will go on record about it. Few content leaders start with that many stories ready to tell.

  • First in the seat. You'll be our first content hire, joining alongside a new Head of Product Marketing and Head of Growth. You'll decide what Outmarket sounds and looks like.

  • Real creative room, and a budget to use it. There's budget for specialist contractors such as editors, shooters and designers, and you'll have room to make work that doesn't look like typical B2B content.

  • A direct line. You'll work with the SVP of Marketing, the founders and customers, and you'll see what your work does for pipeline within weeks.

The role

You own video, social, customer stories and written content. You'll build the function hands-on: you script, interview, direct and write yourself, and you work with a small group of specialist contractors instead of an in-house crew. Pipeline is the team's main number, so success means content that brings brokers into sales conversations, not just views.

Our buyers are owners, producers and operations leaders at commercial insurance agencies. It's a relationship-driven industry, and we're still learning where these buyers spend their attention online. Part of your job is finding out, then making the content that reaches them there.

What you'll do

  • Run the customer story program. Choose which customers to feature with our client services team, plan each story before the shoot, run the interview, and cut one day of filming into pieces for the website, ads, sales and events. Make it easy for busy customers to say yes, and never over-ask the same ones.

  • Ship every week. Build a steady publishing rhythm with a bench of specialist contractors. Find them, brief them clearly, know what things should cost, and review closely so quality holds as volume grows.

  • Turn our events into content. Work with our Director of Industry Events & Programs to plan what to capture at the conferences and customer dinners we already run, and publish soon after.

  • Find where brokers pay attention, whether that's LinkedIn, YouTube, industry media or events. Put our effort where the audience is, not where content teams usually start.

  • Build leaders' voices. Help our founders and other leaders post every week, each in their own voice.

  • Own written content, including the site, social and long-form pieces, and keep everything we publish clear and sharp.

  • Measure what your content does for pipeline and use that to decide what to make next.

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years in B2B content, brand or creative, including time owning a content program end to end.

  • You've personally made content that grew an audience or produced demos and pipeline, and you can explain the numbers and your part in them.

  • You're a hands-on maker. You've scripted, directed, interviewed and edited video and social content yourself, not only managed an agency or writers.

  • You've produced customer stories people actually watch, and you know how to run a great interview.

  • You've shipped on a small budget with contractors and can say what each piece cost.

  • You've built content at an early-stage company, ideally Series A to C, and want to build from scratch again.

  • You're an excellent writer.

How we work

  • High agency: you find the work instead of waiting for it.

  • Ownership: you own the outcome, not a task list.

  • Startup pace: we ship weekly instead of planning quarterly.

You don't need to know insurance. Curiosity about brokers is the requirement, and becoming fluent is part of the job.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/outmarket-ai-head-of-content

jobs.title: Senior Platform Engineer
jobs.description: Headquarters: United States As a Senior Platform Engineer at Coder, you will own the infrastructure Coder's own engineers build on every day. Our internal environments run the same deployment path we publish for customers, so when something does not hold up at our scale, we find it before a customer does. We avoid building anything so specific to ourselves that a customer could not run the same thing. Platform Engineering owns three areas. We run the internal environments our engineers develop in, the self-service environments our field teams use to demo Coder, and the release pipeline that publishes every Coder artifact. You will take ownership of components across these and stay accountable for how they behave in production after they ship. Our users are Coder’s engineers and field teams, and you’ll work with them to decide what to build and how we know it worked. What you'll do here Own one or more components of our Kubernetes platform end to end, from the Terraform and Flux configuration to how they run in production. Improve the platform's observability, so that metrics, logs and alerts land in one stack with a runbook behind every alert. Keep our Kubernetes clusters current, including version and add-on upgrades. Apply cost and performance efficiency to our infrastructure. Work on workspace isolation and container runtimes. Contribute to the release and publishing pipeline for coder/coder, including its workflows, signing and publish targets. Design for least privilege, with short-lived credentials and no shared static keys. Write an RFC when a change warrants one, and a pull request a reviewer can follow without decoding it. Mentor one or two engineers on the components you know best. Run pilots with named users, gather feedback, and measure adoption and time to a useful result (e.g. from request to an environment someone can actually demo on) Own docs, onboarding and support for what you ship. What we're looking for 4+ years in infrastructure or platform engineering, with direct ownership of production systems other people depend on. Strong technical depth across Linux, Kubernetes, containers and Infrastructure as Code, Terraform in particular. Production experience with at least one major public cloud. Most of our infrastructure runs on AWS. Hands-on experience operating Kubernetes clusters, including upgrades, add-ons, autoscaling and the failure modes that come with them. Experience building and owning CI/CD pipelines, and treating them as production software. A working understanding of IP networking and HTTP fundamentals. Has changed or retired a platform feature based on how people used it, or can describe how they would decide to. Good instincts for where cloud spend goes and what a change will cost. Clear written communication. Most of this team's work is agreed in a document before it is built. Bonus tacos if you have (Tacos? If you need an ice-breaker, ask how we say thanks by giving tacos!) GitOps at scale with Flux or Argo CD. Prometheus, Grafana or OpenTelemetry, including alerts you defined and owned. Sandboxed container runtimes such as Kata, gVisor or sysbox. Release engineering, artifact signing or supply chain security. Prior work on developer tooling or internal developer platforms. Public open source contributions. You still carve out time to code, either at work or on passion projects. Our tech stack Backend: Go, Postgres, Kubernetes, gRPC Infrastructure: AWS, Terraform, Flux, Helm Observability: Prometheus, Grafana CI/CD: GitHub Actions General: GitHub, Slack, Discord, Notion About Coder Coder is the leading platform for AI development Infrastructure, enabling enterprises to securely run human and AI-driven development workflows in consistent, governed environments. Coder provides self-hosted, agent-ready workspaces that unify developer productivity and platform governance. With Coder, enterprises can confidently evolve from human-only development to AI-assisted and autonomous workflows, without sacrificing security, compliance, or performance. Learn more at coder.com . Interview process We believe that the interview process should be transparent, consistent, and enjoyable. We value your time and hope to complete the interview process in two to four weeks, if schedules allow. Through your interviews, you will meet a mix of individual contributors, managers, and senior leaders. AI use during the interview process As an AI company, Coder embraces the use of AI tools, and we want to be transparent about our expectations as you navigate our interview process. Not permitted : Using AI assistance during conversational interviews. Permitted : Using AI tooling for take-home assessments. Please flag where and to what extent it was used in your take-home. Your submission will not be penalized for using AI as long as it is done honestly. Our use of AI in hiring We use AI tools to help manage our recruitment process efficiently and fairly. Specifically: Ashby and Brainerr help us review inbound applications by surfacing candidates who best match the role requirements we've defined. This tool does not make hiring decisions; it helps our team prioritize which applications to review first. Granola takes notes during our interview calls so our team can focus on the conversation with you. All hiring decisions are made by humans. Our team reviews applications, conducts interviews, and makes final selections. AI tools assist us but never replace human judgment, and these practices are conducted in compliance with applicable data protection, AI governance, and labor laws. Your data is not used to train AI models. In accordance with New York City Local Law 144, an independent bias audit has been conducted on "Automated Employment Decision Tools"; results are available for Ashby . If you're applying for a role at Coder and have questions about how we use AI in our process, or if you'd like to request information about the data we collect, please contact careers@coder.com . Coder is a proud Equal Opportunity Employer We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to qualified applicants and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, pregnancy, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, marital status, genetic information, disability, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/coder-technologies-inc-senior-platform-engineer

About the Opportunity OKX is hiring a Head of Tax Information Reporting to build and run our global tax information reporting function. The function covers the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF), the EU's DAC8 directive, the amended Common Reporting Standard (CRS 2.0), FATCA, and US Form 1099-DA across multiple reporting entities and a large global user base, with annual reporting across the EU, Brazil, and other CARF jurisdictions. Most of the work is data: getting the right user, transaction, and balance data out of our platform, reconciling it, and turning it into accurate filings. You will own the relationship with our reporting vendor, the data specification that feeds it, and the quality checks that decide whether a file goes out. You will run a central function that owns policy, data, vendor, QA, and submission for every entity in scope. Each reporting entity names an accountable signatory. Local compliance and entity leads are consulted on local requirements and support registration where the law requires a local filer. You will work closely with Product, Data Engineering, Finance Operations, Group Tax, Legal, Data Privacy, and the local entity leads. What You’ll Be Doing Own the end-to-end CARF, DAC8, CRS 2.0, FATCA, and 1099-DA reporting cycle for every OKX entity in scope: population definition, self-certification coverage, data extraction and reconciliation, file production, QA, filing, corrections, and tax authority queries. Define and own the data specification that feeds the tax platform vendor: which users, which transactions, which balances, how they are aggregated by user and jurisdiction, and how they reconcile to the ledger. Work with Product and Data Engineering to build and test the pipeline. Build and run the QA framework. Reconcile every file to source, validate it against the OECD XML schema and local variants, sample-test self-certification reasonableness checks, and run cross-entity consistency checks for users who hold accounts with more than one OKX entity. Nothing files without your release. Manage the tax platform vendor: contract scope, delivery calendar, test cycles, output validation, issue resolution, and the annual renewal decision. Set the group reporting policy and interpret the regimes for OKX: reportable crypto-assets, transfers to unhosted wallets, staking and reward income, retail payment thresholds, residency tie-breakers, and TIN rules, exercising independent technical judgment, supported by Legal and external tax advisers. Own the global tax self-certification design in onboarding, including validation rules, refresh triggers, and the backlog remediation program for existing users, working with Compliance and Product. Define the process for restricting undocumented accounts under DAC8 and CARF, including reason codes and customer communications, with restrictions applied automatically in Product and monitored by the central team. Maintain the entity-by-entity readiness tracker covering domestic enactment, registration, self-certification coverage, and deadlines. Report weekly to the CCO and monthly to the CARF steering committee. Hands-on leader. Build a small, senior team, scaled through the reporting vendor and outside advisers. Coordinate with and train local compliance and entity leads. Support independent testing by Compliance Monitoring, Risk, and Internal Audit, and support tax authority examinations with complete, reproducible records. What We Look For In You 7+ years in tax information reporting, tax operations, or regulatory data reporting at a global exchange, broker, bank, fintech, or digital asset platform, including at least 3 years leading a team. Hands-on experience in a global, distributed digital asset business: you have worked with exchange or wallet transaction data, multiple legal entities, and users spread across many jurisdictions. This is required. Strong data skills. You can write SQL, define data specifications for engineers, reconcile large transaction datasets to a ledger, and find the gap when the numbers do not tie. You have built or run data quality controls on reporting output. Working knowledge of CARF, DAC8, CRS, and FATCA, including due diligence rules, self-certification requirements, reportable transaction categories, and the XML schemas used for exchange. Direct CARF or DAC8 implementation experience is strongly preferred given live DAC8 obligations and upcoming CARF reporting. Experience managing a tax reporting vendor or reporting platform, including scoping, testing, and holding the vendor to a delivery calendar. the tax platform vendor experience is a plus. Experience building a function from a small base: writing the policy, designing the controls, hiring the team, and running the first cycle. Ability to explain data and tax issues plainly to executives, engineers, and local compliance officers, and to run a steering committee. Judgment on when to escalate, comfort working across US, EU, and Asia time zones, and a record of meeting hard filing deadlines. Nice to Haves Experience with US Form 1099-DA or 1099-B production, backup withholding, or Qualified Intermediary reporting. Experience with the DAC8 60-day account restriction process or equivalent undocumented account remediation at scale. Familiarity with GDPR requirements for sharing customer data with tax authorities, including data protection impact assessments. Python or similar scripting for data validation, and experience with data warehouse tools such as Databricks. Experience working inside a Three Lines Model, including supporting second-line monitoring and Internal Audit. A CPA, chartered tax adviser, or equivalent; or a degree in data science, computer science, or accounting. Perks & Benefits Competitive total compensation package L&D programs and Education subsidy for employees' growth and development Various team building programs and company events More that we love to tell you along the process! About the Opportunity OKX is hiring a Head of Tax Information Reporting to build and run our global tax information reporting function. The function covers the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF), the EU's DAC8 directive, the amended Common Reporting Standard (CRS 2.0), FATCA, and US Form 1099-DA across multiple reporting entities and a large global user base, with annual reporting across the EU, Brazil, and other CARF jurisdictions. Most of the work is data: getting the right user, transaction, and balance data out of our platform, reconciling it, and turning it into accurate filings. You will own the relationship with our reporting vendor, the data specification that feeds it, and the quality checks that decide whether a file goes out. You will run a central function that owns policy, data, vendor, QA, and submission for every entity in scope. Each reporting entity names an accountable signatory. Local compliance and entity leads are consulted on local requirements and support registration where the law requires a local filer. You will work closely with Product, Data Engineering, Finance Operations, Group Tax, Legal, Data Privacy, and the local entity leads. Location: remote available, with a strong preference for the US or EU. Some travel to OKX offices. What You'll Be Doing Own the end-to-end CARF, DAC8, CRS 2.0, FATCA, and 1099-DA reporting cycle for every OKX entity in scope: population definition, self-certification coverage, data extraction and reconciliation, file production, QA, filing, corrections, and tax authority queries. Define and own the data specification that feeds the tax platform vendor: which users, which transactions, which balances, how they are aggregated by user and jurisdiction, and how they reconcile to the ledger. Work with Product and Data Engineering to build and test the pipeline. Build and run the QA framework. Reconcile every file to source, validate it against the OECD XML schema and local variants, sample-test self-certification reasonableness checks, and run cross-entity consistency checks for users who hold accounts with more than one OKX entity. Nothing files without your release. Manage the tax platform vendor: contract scope, delivery calendar, test cycles, output validation, issue resolution, and the annual renewal decision. Set the group reporting policy and interpret the regimes for OKX: reportable crypto-assets, transfers to unhosted wallets, staking and reward income, retail payment thresholds, residency tie-breakers, and TIN rules, exercising independent technical judgment, supported by Legal and external tax advisers. Own the global tax self-certification design in onboarding, including validation rules, refresh triggers, and the backlog remediation program for existing users, working with Compliance and Product. Define the process for restricting undocumented accounts under DAC8 and CARF, including reason codes and customer communications, with restrictions applied automatically in Product and monitored by the central team. Maintain the entity-by-entity readiness tracker covering domestic enactment, registration, self-certification coverage, and deadlines. Report weekly to the CCO and monthly to the CARF steering committee. Hands-on leader. Build a small, senior team, scaled through the reporting vendor and outside advisers. Coordinate with and train local compliance and entity leads. Support independent testing by Compliance Monitoring, Risk, and Internal Audit, and support tax authority examinations with complete, reproducible records. What We Look For In You 7+ years in tax information reporting, tax operations, or regulatory data reporting at a global exchange, broker, bank, fintech, or digital asset platform, including at least 3 years leading a team. Hands-on experience in a global, distributed digital asset business: you have worked with exchange or wallet transaction data, multiple legal entities, and users spread across many jurisdictions. This is required. Strong data skills. You can write SQL, define data specifications for engineers, reconcile large transaction datasets to a ledger, and find the gap when the numbers do not tie. You have built or run data quality controls on reporting output. Working knowledge of CARF, DAC8, CRS, and FATCA, including due diligence rules, self-certification requirements, reportable transaction categories, and the XML schemas used for exchange. Direct CARF or DAC8 implementation experience is strongly preferred given live DAC8 obligations and upcoming CARF reporting. Experience managing a tax reporting vendor or reporting platform, including scoping, testing, and holding the vendor to a delivery calendar. the tax platform vendor experience is a plus. Experience building a function from a small base: writing the policy, designing the controls, hiring the team, and running the first cycle. Ability to explain data and tax issues plainly to executives, engineers, and local compliance officers, and to run a steering committee. Judgment on when to escalate, comfort working across US, EU, and Asia time zones, and a record of meeting hard filing deadlines. Nice to Haves Experience with US Form 1099-DA or 1099-B production, backup withholding, or Qualified Intermediary reporting. Experience with the DAC8 60-day account restriction process or equivalent undocumented account remediation at scale. Familiarity with GDPR requirements for sharing customer data with tax authorities, including data protection impact assessments. Python or similar scripting for data validation, and experience with data warehouse tools such as Databricks. Experience working inside a Three Lines Model, including supporting second-line monitoring and Internal Audit. A CPA, chartered tax adviser, or equivalent; or a degree in data science, computer science, or accounting. Perks & Benefits Competitive total compensation package L&D programs and Education subsidy for employees' growth and development Various team building programs and company events Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants More that we love to tell you along the process! jobs.description: Headquarters: United States - Remote, EMEA - Remote Please note that we are unable to consider applications from candidates based in France, Italy, or Germany for this role. Money is moving onto the internet, and the shift has a name: Open Money. This is money that is open, portable, agentic, and owned by you. MetaMask spent the last ten years building it; with 100M+ downloads, users in ~190 countries, and trillions in cumulative transaction volume, it's the most trusted self-custodial financial platform on the internet. Now we're building the operating system for your money: one place to hold, move, grow, and use anything you own. Join a remote-first, global team rebuilding how money works: a problem that touches everyone, every day. About MetaMask & Trade MetaMask is a self-custodial wallet used by tens of millions of people. In Trade, people swap, bridge, trade perps, predict and earn. Core UX is the part of MetaMask mobile that sit inside: Home, the navigation, balances, tokens and positions, and the path from the first screen into each of them. People open the app and land on Home. If that screen is slow, crowded, or unclear about what to do next, Swap, Perps, Predict and Earn see fewer of the people who opened the app. The surface is live. You start from the app people already have, and you keep shipping on it. The role is Staff Product Manager, Core UX. You write the vision for Home and the navigation, and you run the build with design and engineering. A design background is a requirement, because the work is the screen itself. The Role You are the product manager for Core UX on MetaMask mobile. You own the vision, the roadmap and the backlog for Home and the navigation, and you own whether that screen is working. You will work closely with: The Core UX engineering team Design Data and analytics The product managers for Swap, Perps, Predict and Earn Those products show up on Home. You own how a person reaches them from there, and how their balances and positions show up. Their roadmaps stay with their product managers. Yours is Home and the navigation. The app is already live and people open it every day, so you start from what is there. You walk design leadership through the screen, and you are in the reviews where the layout gets decided. What You'll Do Set the Core UX vision Write what Home is for, who has to succeed on it, and what it shows before anyone taps. Getting back to an open position has to be fast for people who already trade here. A first install still has to reach one real action in that same session. Write down where a MetaMask person would already know what to tap, and where one of those apps does something we should study. Then write the roadmap, with the tradeoffs and the order, and what each step changes on Home. Own Home, the navigation and the defaults Own what a person sees when they open the app. That is balances, tokens and positions, and the way into Swap, Perps, Predict and Earn. A balance, a token, a position and an entry point are different, and Home has to show each one in a place the person can find. Decide what Home shows before anyone taps. Anything past that waits until the person opens it. Put Swap, Perps and Predict close together for people who use more than one of them. About MetaMask & Trade

MetaMask is a self-custodial wallet used by tens of millions of people. In Trade, people swap, bridge, trade perps, predict and earn. Core UX is the part of MetaMask mobile that sit inside: Home, the navigation, balances, tokens and positions, and the path from the first screen into each of them.

People open the app and land on Home. If that screen is slow, crowded, or unclear about what to do next, Swap, Perps, Predict and Earn see fewer of the people who opened the app. The surface is live. You start from the app people already have, and you keep shipping on it.

The role is Staff Product Manager, Core UX. You write the vision for Home and the navigation, and you run the build with design and engineering. A design background is a requirement, because the work is the screen itself.

The Role

You are the product manager for Core UX on MetaMask mobile. You own the vision, the roadmap and the backlog for Home and the navigation, and you own whether that screen is working.

You will work closely with:

  • The Core UX engineering team
  • Design
  • Data and analytics
  • The product managers for Swap, Perps, Predict and Earn

Those products show up on Home. You own how a person reaches them from there, and how their balances and positions show up. Their roadmaps stay with their product managers. Yours is Home and the navigation.

The app is already live and people open it every day, so you start from what is there. You walk design leadership through the screen, and you are in the reviews where the layout gets decided.

What You'll Do

Set the Core UX vision

Write what Home is for, who has to succeed on it, and what it shows before anyone taps. Getting back to an open position has to be fast for people who already trade here. A first install still has to reach one real action in that same session.

Write down where a MetaMask person would already know what to tap, and where one of those apps does something we should study. Then write the roadmap, with the tradeoffs and the order, and what each step changes on Home.

Own Home, the navigation and the defaults

Own what a person sees when they open the app. That is balances, tokens and positions, and the way into Swap, Perps, Predict and Earn. A balance, a token, a position and an entry point are different, and Home has to show each one in a place the person can find.

Decide what Home shows before anyone taps. Anything past that waits until the person opens it. Put Swap, Perps and Predict close together for people who use more than one of them. A person using only one of those products still has to be able to finish their action.

Search and any assistance that sits on Home are part of this surface. You specify what stays on the screen, and what the person still confirms before money moves.

Get people to a first action, and get them to come back

You own the first session and the return after it. Count how many new wallets take a real action, and how many of those people open the app again. Define the path from the open to a confirmed action, and instrument it.

Review screens with design

You have a design background, and the role uses it. You review screens for hierarchy, type, spacing and what a tap does. You mark up a screen and say what should change, in writing, so design and engineering can build from the note.

You write the product point of view clearly enough that design and engineering can build it. You are in the design reviews. A crowded screen, or a tap that does the wrong thing, gets the specific change you want.

Work with the products that live on Home

Each MetaMask trade primitive already has their own product manager. You own the entry from Home and the way their positions and balances read there. When a change to Home helps one product and hurts another, you name the tradeoff in the spec.

You coordinate the sequencing when a Home change depends on one of those teams, or when one of their launches depends on Home. The spec says what Home will show on the day their change ships.

Run the work

You take a problem through spec, design, build, test and launch, and then you read what happened. You run planning and the backlog with the Core UX engineering team.

A feature is done when the edge cases are handled, the screen is fast enough to use, and we can see the result in the data. That includes an empty Home, a person who uses one product, and a person who uses several.

When something breaks, you write down what happened and what we will change in the screen or in the process, so the same break has a fix.

Who You Are

You have owned the main screen of a consumer product people open every day, and you stayed on it through launch. You can set a direction for that screen and stay with the tickets until it ships.

You:

  • Mark up a screen and say what the tap should do.
  • Know which KPI a given screen is supposed to impact, and tell a real move from noise.
  • Write a short spec that engineering and design can build, and use that same note when you walk a director through the decision.
  • Sit with someone who already uses the app and someone who just installed, and turn what they do into the next change on Home.
  • Work on a live product, where the screen is already open and the next change has to ship on top of it.

You’ll bring deep technical expertise in at least one area of creative engineering, alongside the curiosity and technical range to work confidently beyond it. You’ll bring deep technical expertise in at least one area of creative engineering, alongside the curiosity and technical range to work confidently beyond it.

A significant amount of our work lives on the internet, so you should be comfortable independently building and shipping highly crafted digital experiences. Other projects may involve hardware, physical computing, unusual displays, installations, or technical systems we haven’t encountered before. You won’t be expected to be an expert in everything, but you should be excited to learn, experiment, and know when to bring in specialists.

Responsibilities

  • Prototype and build highly crafted, experimental digital experiences, interactive projects, and creative tools
  • Work closely with designers and art directors to translate ambitious creative direction into technically excellent experiences, while contributing your own judgment to make the work better
  • Explore emerging technologies and unfamiliar technical approaches, quickly determining what is possible and how best to build it

  • Build and publish standalone web experiences when appropriate, while identifying and communicating the additional engineering support required for more complex projects
  • Experiment with hardware, physical computing, displays, sensors, embedded systems, and other technologies when projects call for them
  • Collaborate with external engineers, fabricators, technical studios, and other specialists, contributing enough technical fluency to be an effective creative and engineering partner
  • Maintain a high bar for performance, reliability, usability, and craft without allowing conventional technical approaches to unnecessarily constrain an idea

 

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 6+ years of relevant software engineering, creative technology, or creative development experience
  • Deep expertise in at least one area of creative engineering, with demonstrated curiosity and competence across adjacent technologies
  • A portfolio of technically ambitious, highly crafted work such as experimental websites, interactive experiences, realtime graphics, games, installations, creative tools, or other unusual applications of technology
  • Strong frontend engineering fundamentals and experience independently building and shipping public-facing web experiences
  • Strong visual and interaction sensibility, with the ability to faithfully execute sophisticated creative direction and identify opportunities to improve it
  • Experience solving unfamiliar technical problems with a high degree of independence
  • Experience writing thoughtful, maintainable code and making pragmatic engineering decisions in fast-moving environments

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with realtime graphics, WebGL, WebGPU, Three.js, shaders, animation, generative systems, or other forms of creative coding
  • Experience working with hardware, physical computing, embedded systems, sensors, displays, Raspberry Pi, Arduino, or interactive installations
  • Familiarity with backend development, APIs, networking, cloud infrastructure, or other areas beyond frontend engineering
  • Experience collaborating with designers, artists, fabricators, creative studios, or other multidisciplinary partners
  • Experience identifying, evaluating, and directing outside technical specialists when a project extends beyond your own expertise
  • Deep curiosity about technology, design, craft, and the ways new technical capabilities can enable new forms of creative work

jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

We are looking for a Senior Manager, 3P Revenue Accounting & Reporting to join our Accounting team. You will own revenue recognition, month-end close and reporting for Claude sold through our cloud service provider (CSP) channels: AWS Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI and Microsoft Azure Marketplace. These channels are among the fastest-growing revenue streams at the company. They run on consumption-based, partner-reported data that changes every month.

You will be the accounting point of contact for the finance and partner teams at AWS, Google and Microsoft. Internally, you will partner with Finance, FAB, Engineering and business teams to turn partner billing feeds into accurate, auditable revenue. You will also lead the automation of a close that is still heavily manual. If you want to build the financial infrastructure behind a fast-growing AI company, come join us in our mission to build safe, beneficial AI.

Key responsibilities

  • Lead the revenue close for cloud service provider Marketplace within a listed company timeline.

  • Prepare and review revenue, revenue-share, reserve journal entries, accruals and true-ups including memos for accounting assessments and judgments.

  • Own balance sheet reconciliations, reserves, and the usage-to-invoice-to-cash bridge.

  • Perform monthly and quarterly flux analysis and prepare flux decks for leadership.

  • Own quarter-end deliverables, including footnote disclosures, flux commentary and presentations to leadership and Corporate Accounting.

  • Serve as the primary contact for external auditors.

  • Review the work of accountants and contractors, set the close calendar, and keep close packages complete and audit-ready.

  • Own monthly and quarterly 3P revenue reporting for leadership and FP&A, by partner, model, product, region and customer.

  • Review partner usage, invoice, disbursement and fraud reports each month, and resolve data issues before close.

  • Serve as the accounting point of contact for the finance, engineering and product teams and drive reporting improvements that support an on-time close.

  • Apply ASC 606 to 3P arrangements, including principal-vs-agent, variable consideration and reseller arrangements.

  • Estimate and document reserves, including credit loss (ASC 326).

  • Assess the accounting for new 3P products, programs and billing changes, partnering with Technical Accounting on complex judgments.

  • Partner with the Engineering teams to automate manual close processes, including SQL-driven workbooks, automated reconciliations and system-generated journal entries.

  • Own 3P SOX controls, including design, documentation, gap remediation and audit evidence.

  • Partner with FP&A, Treasury, AR and business teams on forecasts, cash and partner disputes.

Minimum qualifications

  • Have strong ASC 606 knowledge, especially principal-vs-agent, variable consideration, consideration payable to a customer, and consumption-based revenue.

  • Have owned a month-end close with tight deadlines and reviewed journal entries, reconciliations and flux analysis.

  • Have built revenue reporting from large, imperfect third-party data sets and reconciled it to the general ledger.

  • Have managed external partner relationships where you depended on their data, and pushed for fixes.

  • Have strong SQL skills (BigQuery or similar) and experience automating close workbooks or reconciliations.

  • Have designed or operated SOX controls and supported external audits.

  • Communicate clearly with accounting, finance, business and engineering teams.

  • Thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments where processes are still being built.

Preferred qualifications

  • Have 10+ years of progressive accounting experience, including 3+ years managing revenue accounting or close teams.

  • A Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance; CPA or equivalent (ACA, ACCA).

  • Big 4 audit experience combined with industry experience at a high-growth tech or SaaS company.

  • Experience with cloud marketplace, reseller or channel revenue (AWS Marketplace, Google Cloud Marketplace, Azure Marketplace).

  • Experience with usage-based and subscription revenue models.

  • Hands-on experience with Workday Financials, NetSuite, Numeric, Hex or similar close and reporting tools.

  • Experience with IPO readiness.

  • Experience using AI tools to automate accounting and reporting work.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$190,000—$230,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.
